key_insight: IGA-KAN improves isogeometric PDE solves by fitting local Kolmogorov-Arnold ridge models in closed form on top of an IGA Galerkin solution, rather than replacing the solver.
engineering_relevance: The approach keeps exact CAD geometry and Galerkin structure while boosting accuracy with a non-iterative, error-controlled correction that is attractive for forward and inverse PDE workflows.
method: Compute a baseline IGA Galerkin solution u_h on exact NURBS geometry.
Fit local Kolmogorov-Arnold ridge models on knot-vertex patches using the strong form, boundary data, and u_h via batched linear least squares.
Blend local corrections with IGA hat functions and activate them only where an a posteriori safeguard indicates improvement.
evidence_signal: On eight benchmark problems, the method reduced IGA error by 4.2-90x in L^2 and 4.1-220x in H^1, and recovered an unknown constant source 167x more accurately than IGA in an inverse test.
watch_item: Performance depends on patchwise fitting and safeguard selection, so robustness may vary with mesh resolution, problem smoothness, and the choice of fixed inner functions.
paper_title: IGA-KAN: Isogeometric Analysis with Physics-Informed Closed-Form Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Forward and Inverse PDEs
